effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the reworded text (RP01-EN050, Retro Pack, European release)

transitions.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned while "Toon World" is on your side the field. You can Special Summon this monster from your hand, but Tributes are required for monsters Level 5 or more. This card cannot attack in the turn that it is Summoned. Unless you pay 500 Life Points, this monster cannot attack. When "Toon World" on the field is destroyed, this card is also destroyed. If your opponent doesn't control a Toon Monster, this card can attack your opponent's Life Points directly. If a face-up Toon Monster is on your opponent's side of the field, you must select the Toon Monster as an attack target.
transitions.modern_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned while you control "Toon World". You can Special Summon this card from your hand (but Tributes are required if it is Level 5 or higher). This card cannot attack during the turn it is Summoned. This card cannot attack unless you pay 500 Life Points. When "Toon World" is destroyed, destroy this card. If your opponent doesn't control a Toon Monster, this card can attack your opponent directly. If your opponent controls a face-up Toon Monster, you must select it as an attack target.
transitions.summary: Wording modernisation only: 'while "Toon World" is on your side the field' becomes 'while you control "Toon World"' and the Tribute clause becomes a parenthetical, but the requirement is still level-scaled ('but Tributes are required if it is Level 5 or higher') and the attack lock is still tied to 'the turn it is Summoned'.

transitions.modern_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set. Cannot be Special Summoned unless you control a face-up "Toon World". Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by Tributing the same number of monsters needed for a Tribute Summon (normally 2). This card cannot attack the turn it is Special Summoned. You must pay 500 Life Points to declare an attack with this monster. If "Toon World" on the field is destroyed, destroy this card. This card can attack your opponent directly, unless they control a Toon Monster. If they do control one, this card must target a Toon Monster for its attacks.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the attack lock narrows from 'cannot attack during the turn it is Summoned' to 'cannot attack the turn it is Special Summoned'. The GOAT script encodes the wider lock by cloning the EVENT_SPSUMMON_SUCCESS effect onto EVENT_SUMMON_SUCCESS and EVENT_FLIP_SUMMON_SUCCESS, which is reachable in period play: an opponent's Book of Moon turns the Dragon face-down, and Flip Summoning it back locks its attack under the old text but not under the new one.

transitions.modern_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set. Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by Tributing 2 monsters, while you control "Toon World". transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the Special Summon cost becomes a flat 'by Tributing 2 monsters' instead of 'the same number of monsters needed for a Tribute Summon (normally 2)'. The GOAT script computes the count from the card's current Level ('local amt=(lv>6 and 2) or (lv>4 and 1) or 0'), so with the Level reduced the era card is Special Summoned for 1 Tribute or none; the modern script hard-codes 2 in both its condition and its release selection.

coverage.gap_reason: Project Ignis ships no implementation matching this version: none of the upstream historical variants in the pinned databases carries this version's card text. Reproducing it needs a custom script and a reserved passcode.

review.notes: IMPLEMENTATION GAP is not load-bearing for this project: the version created by the 2012-09-29 erratum (narrow attack lock, still level-scaled Tributes) has no upstream implementation, but it only applies to snapshots between 2012-09-29 and 2015-06-19, and both project snapshots (2005-04-01, 2010-04-24) sit before the whole chain, where the baseline applies. Bug observed in the historical script, worth knowing before anyone tests it: s.spcon computes 'amt=(lv>6 and 2) or (lv>4 and 1) or 0' while s.sptg computes '(lv>6 and 2) or (lv>5 and 1) or 0', so at Level 5 the availability check demands a Tribute the selection step never asks for. Secondary difference not recorded as its own change: the modern attack-lock effect carries EFFECT_FLAG_CANNOT_DISABLE and the goat one does not. Earlier version v0 (MRL-000, 2002-09-16) predates the baseline text and is the pre-Special-Summon-rules wording. Remaining diff is effect renumbering (e1..e7 shifted by one) plus goat's expanded RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END.
